title: Times Tables to 12 × 12 (KS2)
subject: Maths
strapline: Instant recall of all the tables — and the tricks that help.
facts: By the end of Year 4, children are expected to recall all tables up to 12 × 12.
Multiplication is commutative: 7 × 8 = 8 × 7, so learning one fact gives you two.
The 9 times table: the tens digit goes up and the ones digit goes down (09, 18, 27, 36...).
The 4 times table is double-double: 4 × 6 = double 6, then double again = 24.
The 11 times table up to 9: just repeat the digit — 11 × 3 = 33, 11 × 7 = 77.
Every fact has a division partner: 6 × 7 = 42, so 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
Square numbers appear on the diagonal: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36... (a number times itself).
teacher_tips: Focus practice on the few facts a child doesn't yet know, not the whole grid.
Teach the commutative shortcut so the "hard" facts halve in number.
Mix multiplication and division questions so facts are flexible.
